planting.note: Plant tubers in spring after the last frost when soil has warmed to at least 65 degrees F; Torago is a vigorous, sun-tolerant strap-leaf caladium with a bright red center bleeding into a wide green margin.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to sun with regular overhead protection from the hottest afternoon exposure; strap-leaf types like Torago hold color and resist scorch far better than fancy-leaf caladiums when given consistent moisture. Torago produces narrow, upright leaves with a vivid red center that fades through pink veining into a broad green edge, giving strong color from a distance in beds and mass plantings. It is a heavier feeder than dwarf caladiums, so an organic mulch and periodic light fertilizing keeps leaf color saturated through the season; dig and store tubers before the first fall frost outside zone 9b and warmer.

planting.note: Plant tubers in spring after the last frost once soil has warmed to at least 65 degrees F; Tapestry is a sun-tolerant lance-leaf caladium with deep wine-purple leaves flecked in rose-pink and edged in green.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to sun with consistent watering; deeper leaf colors like Tapestry's benefit from a little morning sun to intensify pigment without the fading heavy shade can cause. Tapestry carries lance-shaped leaves in a rich wine-purple heavily speckled with rose-pink and rimmed in green, a moodier palette than the classic red or white caladiums that pairs well with chartreuse or silver-leaved companions. It multiplies steadily from year to year where tubers overwinter in the ground; elsewhere lift clumps after foliage yellows in fall and store dry tubers above 60 degrees F until spring.

common_name: Desert Sunset Caladium (Coral-Pink Sun-Tolerant Lance-Leaf Caladium)

planting.note: Plant tubers in spring after the last frost once soil has warmed to at least 65 degrees F; Desert Sunset is a sun-tolerant lance-leaf caladium with a coral-pink to salmon center shading to a green margin.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to sun with reliable irrigation during hot weather; the warm coral tones of Desert Sunset read best with some direct morning light and afternoon shade in Gulf South gardens. Leaves emerge coral-pink to salmon at the center, softening through blush tones before meeting a clean green edge, giving a warmer color echo than the typical red-and-green caladium palette. It combines well with purple-leaved sweet potato vine and dark-foliaged coleus in mixed containers; where winters stay above 50 degrees F tubers can remain in the ground under mulch, otherwise lift and store indoors over winter.

common_name: Strawberry Star Caladium (Pink-Speckled Sun-Tolerant Lance-Leaf Caladium)

planting.note: Plant tubers in spring after the last frost once soil has warmed to at least 65 degrees F; Strawberry Star is a sun-tolerant lance-leaf caladium with rose-pink speckling over green that intensifies toward the leaf center.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to sun with consistent moisture through summer heat; the fine pink speckling of Strawberry Star shows up best against its green background when plants get a few hours of direct sun. Narrow, upright lance leaves are heavily dusted with rose-pink spots that coalesce toward a soft pink midrib, giving a lighter, airier look than the bold-blotched fancy-leaf types. Its compact habit suits the front of a shaded border, window boxes, and mixed containers; dig and dry tubers before frost outside the warmest zones for replanting the following spring.

common_name: Cranberry Star Caladium (Dark Red Compact Sun-Tolerant Caladium)

planting.note: Plant tubers in spring after the last frost once soil has warmed to at least 65 degrees F; Cranberry Star is a compact, sun-tolerant strap-leaf caladium with deep cranberry-red leaves rimmed in green.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to sun with even moisture; compact strap-leaf caladiums like Cranberry Star tolerate more direct light than fancy-leaf types and hold their dwarf habit even in richer soil. Leaves are a deep, saturated cranberry-red with a narrow green edge, staying low and dense rather than upright, which makes it useful for edging beds and filling small pots. It pairs well with silver or chartreuse companions that set off the dark color; in zone 9 and warmer, tubers can often overwinter in the ground under heavy mulch, while colder gardens should lift and store tubers indoors once foliage dies back.
